problem: The weight $w,$ in pounds, of a baby gorilla $t$ years after birth can be modeled by the function $w(t)=4{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}+15.$ What is the instantaneous rate of change of his weight when $t=1$ year?

examples.knowledge_point: Determining a Rate of Change for a Given Function at a Point
examples.problem: Lizzie buys $b$ pounds of bananas at a price $p,$ in dollars, that can be modeled by the function $p(b)=5e^{-0.2b}.$ What is the instantaneous rate of change of the price when $b=5$ pounds?
examples.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the price when $b=5$ pounds is equal to $p'(5).$

First, we take the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(b) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}b}(5{e}^{-0.2b}) \\  & =5{e}^{-0.2b}\cdot (-0.2) \\  & =-{e}^{-0.2b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $b=5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(5) & =-{e}^{-0.2(5)} \\  & =-{e}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{e}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate change of the price when $b=5$ pounds is $-\dfrac{1}{e}$ dollars per pound.

feedback.problem:
The function $C(t)=6{e}^{-2t}$ gives the concentration, in milligrams per liter, of a medication in the bloodstream $t$ hours after administration. Find the instantaneous rate of change of the concentration as a function of $t.$

The instantaneous rate of change of the concentration is
{{field-1}}
milligrams per liter per hour.
feedback.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the concentration is equal to ${C}^{′}(t).$

Now, the rate of change of $C(t)$ with respect to $t$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{e}^{-2t}) \\  & =6(-2){e}^{-2t} \\  & =-12{e}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change of the concentration is $-12{e}^{-2t}$ milligrams per liter per hour.
